commit.message:
deploy: the per-deploy gate is code now

One day of agent-run verification made the case plainly: every check on the
happy path was mechanical — poll to terminal, compare the serving commit,
probe the URL and match the marker, read verificationStatus, diff live config
against what the repo declares — and every failure the agent hit was sandbox
friction, not a deploy problem. In this system gates are deterministic and
agents do judgment work; deploy verification is a gate, and now it runs as
one: tools/deploy-verify/index.mjs, dependency-free, seconds per deploy, and
RENDER_API_KEY never enters an LLM environment at all.

The role survives intact — same release records, same contract, same draft
promotion PR on healthy staging deploys, same backward-only rollback on
failed production ones, opened issues included. The charter stays as the
rulebook and now says so in a banner: an agent reading it is being summoned
for an audit or a triage, never a routine deploy.

The tool carries a fixtures mode (DEPLOY_VERIFY_FIXTURES) that replaces API
reads with files and disables every side effect, so the full decision path —
live, failed-with-rollback, degraded-with-drift — is tested offline against
the API shapes the agent runs left behind in pipeline/releases/evidence.
deploy.config.json gains serviceName so the rename class of drift the agent
caught tonight stays caught. The workflow drops the Claude CLI install, needs
only RENDER_API_KEY, finishes in seconds, and goes red on a failed outcome
after committing the record.

Co-Authored-By: claude-flow <ruv@ruv.net>
